q: In chemical calculations, chemists use relative masses of atoms and molecules on the basis of a designated standard unit mass, called _____.
e: In chemical calculations, chemists use relative masses of atoms and molecules on the basis of a designated standard unit mass, called atomic mass unit (amu). Atomic mass unit (amu) is the idea that completes this fact. Molar mass would fill a different blank than atomic mass unit (amu).

q: Scientists have chosen to use the isotope _____ as the new standard because it is the most abundant isotope.
e: Scientists have chosen to use the isotope carbon-12 as the new standard because it is the most abundant isotope. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. Carbon-14 would fill a different blank than carbon-12.

q: The relative atomic mass of an element is the average mass of one atom of the element compared with _____ the mass of one atom of the carbon-12 isotope.
e: The relative atomic mass of an element is the average mass of one atom of the element compared with one twelfth the mass of one atom of the carbon-12 isotope. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. One tenth would fill a different blank than one twelfth.

q: Atomic mass unit (amu) is precisely _____ the mass of one atom of carbon-12.
e: Atomic mass unit (amu) is precisely one twelfth the mass of one atom of carbon-12. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. One quarter would fill a different blank than one twelfth.

q: To calculate the relative atomic mass of an element, we must know the isotopic masses of the various isotopes present and the _____ of the isotopes in nature.
e: To calculate the relative atomic mass of an element, we must know the isotopic masses of the various isotopes present and the relative abundance of the isotopes in nature. Relative abundance is the idea that completes this fact. Molecular mass would fill a different blank than relative abundance.

q: The relative molecular mass ($M_r$) of a molecule is the mass of one molecule of a substance on a scale where the carbon-12 isotope has a mass of exactly _____ units.
e: The relative molecular mass (M_r) of a molecule is the mass of one molecule of a substance on a scale where the carbon-12 isotope has a mass of exactly 12 units. Carbon-12 is the mass standard: one-twelfth of that atom is the atomic mass unit. 1 would fill a different blank than 12.

q: For ionic compounds, such as sodium chloride and magnesium oxide, we use the term _____ instead of relative molecular mass.
e: For ionic compounds, such as sodium chloride and magnesium oxide, we use the term relative formula mass instead of relative molecular mass. Relative formula mass is the idea that completes this fact. Empirical formula would fill a different blank than relative formula mass.

q: Ionic compounds consist of _____ and not molecules.
e: Ionic compounds consist of ions and not molecules. Ions is the idea that completes this fact. Electrons is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: The relative atomic mass ($A_r$) is used to represent the mass of an atom of an element because the size of an atom is too small to be _____.
e: The relative atomic mass (A_r) is used to represent the mass of an atom of an element because the size of an atom is too small to be weighed practically. Weighed practically is the idea that completes this fact. Seen under a microscope would fill a different blank than weighed practically.

q: The relative molecular mass ($M_r$) can be found by adding up the _____ of all the atoms present in the molecule.
e: The relative molecular mass (M_r) can be found by adding up the atomic numbers of all the atoms present in the molecule. Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus, and it identifies the element. Oxidation numbers would fill a different blank than atomic numbers.
